config.httpPort.description: Local HTTP port (1–65535). Must differ from debugPort. The managed runtime uses no AJP/HTTPS connector.
config.debugPort.description: JPDA debug port (the port VS Code attaches to)
config.javaOpts.description: `JAVA_OPTS` environment variable passed to the JVM when Tomcat starts.
config.colorizeLogs.description:
Colorize log output by level (PowerShell on Windows, AWK on macOS/Linux).  
🟣 `FATAL/CRITICAL` → Magenta  
🔴 `ERROR/SEVERE/Exception` → Red  
🟡 `WARN/WARNING` → Yellow  
🟠 `SQL/Hikari/Query` → DarkYellow  
🟢 `HTTP/Mapping/Dispatching` → Green  
🔵 `INFO/Started` → Cyan  
🔹 `DEBUG` → Blue  
👤 `TRACE` → DarkCyan
config.autoOpenBrowser.description: Open the application URL when the HTTP port starts accepting connections. This checks the port, not application health. Cancels when the debug session ends.
config.showStatusBar.description: Show the Tomcat shortcut menu in the status bar.

config.jndi.title: Happy Spring Tomcat - JNDI
config.jndiResources.description:
Optional JNDI resources for local debugging, such as a database DataSource. Leave `[]` if META-INF/context.xml already supplies the required resources. Settings replace the complete same-named Resource definition; include all required attributes. Duplicate names within settings are rejected.

Edit in `settings.json`, then run **Apply Debug Setup** and restart Tomcat. Example for Oracle with Tomcat DBCP2 (replace the name, URL and credentials for your project):
```json
{
  "happySpringTomcat.jndiResources": [
    {
      "name": "jdbc/myDB",
      "auth": "Container",
      "type": "javax.sql.DataSource",
      "factory": "org.apache.tomcat.dbcp.dbcp2.BasicDataSourceFactory",
      "driverClassName": "oracle.jdbc.OracleDriver",
      "url": "jdbc:oracle:thin:@localhost:1521:ORCL",
      "username": "YOUR_DB_USER",
      "password": "YOUR_DB_PASSWORD",
      "maxTotal": 20,
      "maxIdle": 5,
      "maxWaitMillis": 10000
    }
  ]
}
```
`name` must match the application's JNDI lookup; `jdbc/myDB` is available as `java:comp/env/jdbc/myDB`. Make the JDBC driver JAR available to Tomcat, for example in Tomcat Home's `lib` directory. DBCP2 uses `maxTotal` and `maxWaitMillis`; custom factories may use different attributes.

config.builtWebAppDirectory.description: Built web application directory containing WEB-INF/lib. Leave empty for automatic detection during Setup. Example: `${workspaceFolder}/target/exploded` (use your project's actual build output). Supplies dependency JARs and built META-INF/context.xml. Relative paths resolve from the project folder. [Select folder...](command:happy-spring-tomcat.selectBuiltWebAppDirectory)
config.webSourceDirectory.description: Web sources containing JSP, static files and WEB-INF/web.xml. Normally `${workspaceFolder}/src/main/webapp`. Changes are read directly without rebuilding the WAR. This is not the Java source directory. Use an empty string to disable the web source mapping.
config.classesDirectory.description: Directory containing compiled .class files. Maven normally uses `${workspaceFolder}/target/classes`; Gradle normally uses `${workspaceFolder}/build/classes/java/main`. Use your actual build or IDE output. For Hot Code Replace, the Java IDE must update the same runtime output. Empty means use classes from the complete built web application.
config.preLaunchBuild.description: Build to run before Tomcat starts. Default none leaves compilation and resource processing to the IDE or user. Set the runtime directories to the selected builder’s actual output. Run Setup after changing this setting.
config.preLaunchBuild.none: Do not run a build. The IDE or user must prepare classes and resources.
config.preLaunchBuild.maven: Run Maven compile for mapped classes/resources, or package for a complete built webapp. Prefer the Maven Wrapper. For resource processing only, use a custom VS Code task running mvn process-resources.
config.preLaunchBuild.gradle: Run Gradle classes for mapped output. Set Classes Directory and Resources Directory to the project’s output paths. For a complete built webapp, build the WAR and sync it into the selected separate folder under the Gradle build directory. Prefer the Gradle Wrapper.
config.preLaunchBuild.custom: Run the existing VS Code task named in Custom Build Task.
config.customBuildTask.description: VS Code task label used only when Pre Launch Build is custom, e.g. Local Maven Build. Define the command and arguments in tasks.json (e.g. mvn compile -Plocal). This is a task label, not a shell command or Maven goal. The task must finish and prepare the directories configured below. Existing user tasks are preserved.
config.resourcesDirectory.description: Optional separate directory containing processed XML/properties. Maven normally includes them in Classes Directory, so leave this empty. Standard Gradle output uses `${workspaceFolder}/build/resources/main`; set that path when resources are separate. Requires Classes Directory. This maps existing output and does not copy or build resources.
